title: La Danta pyramid, El Mirador
summary: La Danta is a Preclassic Maya pyramid at El Mirador in the Petén region of northern Guatemala. Guinness World Records gives it a height of up to 72 m on a footprint of about 500 by 300 m, built between 300 BCE and 150 CE. A Yale eHRAF Archaeology abstract places the major structures at El Mirador in the Late Preclassic.

uncertainty.note: Start is 300 BCE (astronomical -299) from Guinness World Records, which says the pyramid was built between 300 BCE and 150 CE; the Yale eHRAF abstract says only Late Preclassic. End is the present: the ruin still stands (Guinness: rising above the canopy).

as_recorded.value: All of the major structures appear to be from the Late Preclassic.

importance.justification: Guinness World Records lists it as the largest Maya pyramid by volume (about 2.8 million m3).
